knowledge.title: Where these numbers come from
knowledge.subtitle: A short explanation behind every number on the nutrition page — nothing mysterious, just standard formulas widely used, not an AI guess.
knowledge.footer: All numbers are estimates from standard formulas, not medical advice — if you have a specific health condition, consult a doctor or dietitian.
knowledge.bmrP1: BMR is the energy your body burns even without moving at all (breathing, pumping blood, etc). Calculated with the Mifflin-St Jeor formula, which current nutrition guidelines consider the most accurate for most people (more accurate than the older Harris-Benedict formula).
knowledge.bmrP2: If you have an InBody scan (or other body composition device) logged on the nutrition page, the app switches to the Katch-McArdle formula instead, which is more accurate than Mifflin-St Jeor because it's based on your actual Lean Body Mass from the scan, instead of estimating from population averages of weight/height/age/sex.
knowledge.bmrFormulaLbm: Lean Body Mass (LBM) = weight from scan(kg) × (1 − body fat% from scan ÷ 100)
knowledge.bmrP3: Only uses the most recent scan that has a body fat% value — if you haven't logged a scan yet, or logged one without body fat%, the Mifflin-St Jeor formula above is used as usual instead.
knowledge.tdeeP1: BMR multiplied by a factor based on your everyday activity level — activities logged in the app aren't counted again on top of this, since the multiplier already covers your overall lifestyle.
knowledge.goalP1: 1 kg of body fat ≈ 7,700 kcal — this is the standard figure used to calculate how much of a daily surplus/deficit you need to change weight at your chosen rate.
knowledge.goalP2: Calorie target = TDEE ± this difference (add if gaining, subtract if losing), and it will never recommend below 1,200 kcal/day no matter how aggressive a loss rate you set — that's a minimum safety floor, not an amount actually recommended to eat. If you need to eat less than that, it should be under a doctor's supervision.
macroList: Protein (no InBody scan): 1.8 grams per kg of body weight (mid-range of the 1.6-2.2 g/kg recommended for people who exercise regularly)

Protein (with an InBody scan that has body fat%): 2.4 grams per kg of Lean Body Mass (LBM) — the top end of the 2.0-2.4 g/kg LBM range sports research recommends, since the actual fat/muscle split is known, no need to buffer for the error margin of a bodyweight-only formula
Carbs: whatever's left after protein and fat
knowledge.macroExample: Example: 70.1 kg body weight, 19.3% body fat → LBM ≈ 56.6 kg → protein target ≈ 56.6 × 2.4 ≈ 136 g/day (higher than a bodyweight-only calculation, since it's now known exactly how much of that weight is muscle/organs that actually need protein)
knowledge.waterP1: This is the midpoint of the commonly used 30-35 mL/kg range.
knowledge.activityTitle: Why today's activity increases your targets
knowledge.activityP1: A day with an activity logged (from Strava or manually) automatically bumps up your targets, counted in 30-minute blocks:
activityList: Water: +500 mL per 30 min (up to +1.5 L/day)
Carbs: +15 g per 30 min (up to +90 g/day) — replenishing used glycogen
Protein: +5 g per 30 min (up to +30 g/day)
knowledge.activityP2: Calculated from duration alone, not split by intensity, since manually logged activities don't have intensity data comparable to activities synced from Strava — so the same formula works for both.
knowledge.weightTitle: What the weight trend chart is for
knowledge.weightP1: Logging your weight on the nutrition page automatically updates your profile's weight, so BMR/TDEE always calculate from your latest weight without having to go back and edit it on the settings page each time.
